avis.titre: BE AWARE of the Strong Mint Scent & Cooling!
avis.texte: I purchased this Osea Cleansing Mudd on sale, having used and enjoyed the brands Ocean cleanser many times before. I am personally enjoying it for the most part so far, but wanted to share some important information that's not entirely clear on the product description or ingredients. The ingredients list for this product (both on the Ulta site and Osea's own site) does not explicitly list that it includes a mint oil, which gives it both a strong scent and also the potential to be irritating to some people. It's just listed as "fragrance / parfum*" and it's fairly high up in the ingredient list (meaning there's a higher concentration of it as ingredients are listed in order of % of the formula they comprise). For me, personally, it's usually a strong cooling effect, but even using it on my cheeks below my eyes can make my eyes feel whiffs of the peppermint oil. I'm not putting it on or near my eyes (as you shouldn't and the bottle clearly says so), the mint is just that strong. If you double cleanse and use the same cleanser both times, you may not want to do that with this one as it can then start to feel irritating or drying on the skin. I have combination, acne-prone skin that can be sensitive but I wouldn't call it very sensitive. The cooling sensation of this cleanser can feel very nice after something like a workout or just a really warm day. Be sure to rinse it off thoroughly to stop the cooling sensation!

avis.titre: Mint Overload Ruins an Otherwise Lovely Mask
avis.texte: Out with the old. I used La Mer for decades, but in my mid-40s, during perimenopause, Ive become more aware of endocrine disruptors in skincare. I was disappointed to learn that, despite its steep price, La Mer is not a clean brand. As someone who has battled hormonal imbalance and fibroids for years, I assumed premium meant safer ingredients - unfortunately, it didnt. Ive since moved to OSEA I love my facials, every Friday is spa day so I was excited to try this face polish deep cleansing mask after switching to clean products. The texture is beautiful, and it feels nice initially, but the mint essential oil is far too intense. With my compromised skin barrier, it stung badly and even brought me to tears. On a hot summer day, the cooling effect was pleasant, but the sting outweighed it. If you have sensitive , sensitized or damaged skin, avoid this. I wish there were a reduced mint or fragrance-free option Ill jump on it.
